summary: William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Joe Bransford Wilson, and later held posts at Virginia, Dharma Drum Institute, and Chung-Hwa Institute.
William Blackstone was an English scholar who studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford. He subsequently held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1758 to 1766.

William C. Kirby is a sinologist and historian. Educated at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn, he taught at Washington University in St. Louis (1980–1992) before serving at Harvard from 1992 as Dean and Fairbank Center Director (circa 2006–2013).

William Carey was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College in 1801 and founded Serampore College and the Baptist Missionary Society.

William Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tehran, he held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, SUNY, and Stony Brook University from circa 1983.

William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Williams, Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, and in Germany under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and served as a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

William Erskine was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1787 to 1792.
William Evans Hoyle was a British scholar who completed his studies at the Victoria University of Manchester from circa 1872 to 1874 and at Christ Church from circa 1874 to 1877.

William F. Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. His career includes posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was attested in 1986 and as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Bonn. He held visiting positions at several universities before serving as full professor and Halls-Bascom Professor of Classical Chinese Literature at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1983.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge from circa 1921 to 1925. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1932 to 1969.

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University, including Harvard Medical School, he held successive posts at Harvard starting in 1872, serving as Professor from 1885.

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College, Oxford, and Middle Temple. He became Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in 1783 and founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Collett Cox, later holding posts at Washington, California Institute of Integral Studies, and JFK University.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, he taught at Davidson and served at UCLA from circa 1992, becoming Professor Emeritus around 2021.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Connecticut College and completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by David Germano.
William P. Chu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles, by 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.
